result.summary: Removes the `noexcept` specification from `SaltedOutpointHasher::operator()` to induce `libstdc++`'s `std::unordered_map` to cache hash codes within node structures. This effectively reverts PR #16957, trading a node-size memory increase of one `size_t` for reduced SipHash recomputations during UTXO map operations. A unit test is also added to check invocability and the `libstdc++` fast-hash trait.
result.problem: In `libstdc++`, `std::unordered_map` omits cached hash codes in bucket nodes when the hash functor is marked `noexcept`, forcing table lookups and rehashing in `CCoinsMap` to repeatedly recompute outpoint hashes with SipHash. While PR #16957 introduced `noexcept` to reduce memory usage per node by about 9%, it introduced a runtime penalty.
evidence: Author's benchmarks show reindex-chainstate and IBD completing approximately 2% to 3% faster with cached hash codes across different `-dbcache` settings.
Author reports up to ~11% speedup during AssumeUTXO loading (`loadtxoutset`), which isolates the coins cache performance from block validation overhead.
Author's Massif profiling showed memory usage was roughly neutral at moderate `-dbcache` values, but increased at very high cache sizes (24.11 GB to 25.49 GB peak RSS).
result.scope_notes: Relies on implementation-defined behavior in libstdc++ where non-noexcept fast hash functions cause unordered containers to store cached hash values in nodes. The unit test uses the internal libstdc++ header `<bits/functional_hash.h>` and `std::__is_fast_hash` under `__GLIBCXX__`.
result.card: This PR marks SaltedOutpointHasher as noexcept(false) to prompt libstdc++ unordered containers to cache hash codes in their nodes. This intentionally reverses the tradeoff made in PR #16957, prioritizing CPU speed over per-node memory savings in the UTXO cache. The author's benchmarks demonstrate a 2% to 3% runtime improvement during IBD and reindex-chainstate, and up to an 11% speedup during AssumeUTXO loading, at the cost of higher peak memory on very large dbcache configurations.
